verdict.rationale: First-party docs state the Supabase CLI runs the entire Supabase stack locally or in CI with `supabase init` and `supabase start`, and a hands-on user confirms `supabase start` spins up a Docker instance from migration files. Mixed community reports (one easy local setup, one team that couldn't get local dev working) lower confidence in reliability but don't concretely refute the capability. missing for 10: a documented per-service breakdown of what runs locally (auth, storage, functions, realtime), consistent independent corroboration that local dev works smoothly.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole backend stack locally with an emulator or CLI before deploying

citations.quote: The Supabase CLI enables you to run the entire Supabase stack locally, on your machine or in a CI environment.
The Supabase CLI runs the entire Supabase stack on your own machine or in a CI environment, so you can build and test locally, then connect your project to a hosted one
`supabase start` to launch the Supabase services
